description: Tremolo Vast is a gas giant that breaks every expectation set by its class. Where most such worlds present in bands of ochre, cream, and rust, Tremolo Vast is overwhelmingly, impossibly green — its atmosphere saturated with methane compounds and trace organics that absorb red light and scatter emerald hues across its cloud tops. Even its ring system shimmers green, composed of ice crystals tinted by the same atmospheric chemistry that colors the planet itself.

The planet earned its designation from the trembling radio signal it broadcasts into surrounding space, a natural phenomenon created by atmospheric acoustic waveguides that trap and modulate electromagnetic emissions into an oscillating pulse. Early survey ships mistook the signal for an artificial beacon and spent months searching for its source. The sound, when converted to audio, resembles a vast and endless tremolo — a wavering note sustained across the void.

No satisfactory explanation exists for Tremolo Vast's unusual coloration. Standard atmospheric models cannot account for the specific combination of compounds present, and spectral analysis has identified at least three molecular species not found in any other known gas giant. Some researchers have proposed that the planet formed around an unusual protoplanetary seed, possibly extragalactic in origin. Others suggest the chemistry is being actively maintained by some unknown process deep within the atmosphere.

Tremolo Vast's commercial value as a fuel depot is considerable, but its scientific mystery is what draws the most attention. Three research stations maintain permanent orbit, their crews monitoring the atmospheric chemistry for changes that might explain the planet's anomalous composition. The tremolo signal has recently begun shifting in frequency for the first time in recorded history, and no one can agree on whether this is a natural fluctuation or something responding to the increased presence of observers.
